comments.author: @ScottCheggers
comments.text:
So the graphic showing where different Scandinavians went is a little over simplified for the UK and Ireland. The Danes only really went to England, they didn’t come to Ireland or Scotland (they might have went to Wales, I’m not sure). For us in Scotland and Ireland, it was mostly Norwegians, for example in Ireland it was Norwegians who founded Dublin (there was another Irish settlement nearby that’s part of the modern city, but the port and original town are Norwegian) while in Scotland the Western Isles (The Hebrides), the northern tip (Caithness), Orkney and Shetland (the northern Isles) were all part of Norway for a very long time. The heir to the Norwegian throne was the Lord of the Isles, hell we only took Orkney and Shetland from Norway in 1472 (they were given as a dowry). 

Today there’s a reconstruction movement to revive the traditional language in Orkney and Shetland which was called Norn while the modern reconstruction is called Nynorn. And there’s a pretty small movement to rejoin Norway
